questions.question: A tuck shop takes R2 375 on Monday and R1 860 on Tuesday. Find the total and the difference, showing one check for each.
questions.expected_answer: Total: 2 375 plus 1 860 is 4 235, so R4 235; estimate 2 400 plus 1 900 is 4 300, close. Difference: 2 375 minus 1 860 is 515, so R515 more on Monday; check 1 860 plus 515 is 2 375.

questions.question: A fence needs 1 250 metres of wire and 865 metres have been used. Work out how much more is needed by rounding and compensating, and explain the unit in the answer.
questions.expected_answer: 1 250 minus 900 is 350; 900 is 35 more than 865, so 35 too much was taken away and is added back: 385. Both numbers were metres, so the answer is 385 metres.

questions.question: Describe the four-step routine for a word problem and explain how the last step would catch an impossible answer about filling a 5 000 litre tank.
questions.expected_answer: Read and picture the problem; write the number sentence with a box; calculate with one technique and check with another; write the answer with its unit and reread the question. If the answer to how much more water fills the tank came out above 5 000 litres, the tank would overflow, so the sentence must have been wrong, and the last step sends you back.
